bull.t: Strong Revenue Growth and Gross-Margin Improvement
bull.b: The combination of strong trailing revenue growth and materially higher gross margin indicates improved commercial scale and product economics. If sustained, this gives Take-Two more resources to fund game development, marketing, and live-service investment while supporting better operating leverage.

Large, enduring franchises provide Take-Two with established demand, global brand recognition, and recurring monetization opportunities across new releases and live services. Strong NBA 2K engagement and continued GTA momentum support the durability of the company’s content ecosystem.

bull.t: Improving Cash Generation and Financial Position
bull.b: Positive operating and free cash flow represent a meaningful recovery from prior negative periods and improve the company’s ability to finance development internally. Management’s expectation of over $1 billion operating cash flow and year-end net cash would further strengthen financial flexibility.

bear.b: Revenue and gross-margin gains have not yet translated into consistent bottom-line profitability. Continued operating and net losses limit internal compounding, make results more dependent on successful releases, and leave less tolerance for development delays, weaker engagement, or cost increases.

Mobile is an important part of Take-Two’s portfolio, so declining bookings and higher user-acquisition pressure could weigh on recurring growth and monetization efficiency. Moderation in mature Zynga titles may require continued investment in new games to replace slowing contributions.

bear.t: Higher Costs and Content Impairment Pressure Margins
bear.b: Higher cost of revenue and an impairment tied to a canceled title show that content development and portfolio management can create meaningful earnings volatility. Repeated execution issues or weaker project economics could delay the company’s transition from growth to durable profitability.
